answer: Agents mitigate Sybil attacks via memory-hard delay functions. To maintain an identity, a node continuously computes memory-bound proofs, forcing attackers to dedicate physical SRAM channels and power per identity. Assuming software can bypass this hardware cost is an engineering fable. Epochal decay prevents any dormant credential from persisting as a relic. However, deploying updates via a velvet fork creates temporary validation latency disparities across peers.
